title: Warren Buffett: 99% of His Fortune Came After 52
description:
Forbes put Warren Buffett's net worth at $250 million in 1982, when he was 52. On Nov 1, 2026, at 96, Forbes estimated about $154 billion: 616 times more, so over 99% of today's fortune came after 52 (and that is after giving away roughly $60 billion since 2006). That is like growing about 15.7% a year for 44 years, doubling roughly every 4.7 years. The late boom came from an early start: he bought his first stock at 11. His returns were exceptional; the lesson is time in compounding, not copying him.

Sources: Forbes 400 (1982), as reported by Forbes (Dec 9, 2016; Sept 28, 2022; Oct 5, 2024); Forbes real-time ranking as of Nov 1, 2026 (reported by Forbes Argentina, Nov 2, 2026); Berkshire Hathaway 2018 shareholder letter (Feb 2019); Associated Press (June 30, 2025) on gifts since 2006. The growth curve shown is a smoothed illustration, not his actual yearly path. Net worth estimates move daily. Educational content, not investment advice; past returns don't predict future returns.

scenes.say: In nineteen eighty-two, at fifty-two, Forbes put his net worth at two hundred and fifty million dollars. In November twenty twenty-six: about one hundred and fifty-four billion.
That's like growing about sixteen percent a year for forty-four years. Smoothed out, the curve looks flat for decades, then shoots up.
At that pace, money doubles roughly every five years. After nine doublings, the final doubling alone added about seventy-seven billion dollars.
And that late boom came from an early start: he bought his first stock at eleven.
His returns were exceptional, and nobody can count on them. The real lesson is time: start early, and give compounding decades to work.
